name: close
description: The close() system call closes a file descriptor, making it no longer refer to any file and allowing it to be reused. Any record locks owned by the process on the associated file are removed. If it is the last file descriptor referring to the file, the resources are freed.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: fd isn’t a valid open file descriptor.
The close() call was interrupted by a signal; see signal(7).
On NFS, may be reported against close() if storage space is exceeded.
On NFS, may be reported against close() if quota is exceeded.

bugs: Do not retry close() after an error as it may lead to undefined behavior; be cautious with file descriptors in multithreaded processes due to potential race conditions.
